document: Roadmap — queued changes after initial deploy

status_legend.queued: Captured and specced, brief not yet written

notes: Briefs are sequenced to respect dependencies and to keep each merge reviewable.
Each brief produces multiple commits (one per phase within the brief).
Brief 001 is already complete and deployed.
Brief 002 has been written; remaining briefs are specced but not yet drafted.
CRM module is captured separately in docs/FUTURE_CRM.md and is not part of this roadmap.
Each change carries a 'principles' field that must be enforced when its brief is written, so Claude Code does not quietly expand scope.

briefs.title: Header restructure, customisable dashboard, bigger mobile tabs
briefs.rationale: Make the app feel personal (business name in header), give each user control over their own dashboard, and fix the mobile tap-target problem.

phases.name: Header restructure
phases.summary: Move business name + page title inline with avatar; remove standalone heading block from each page body.

phases.name: Bigger mobile bottom tabs
phases.summary: 72px tab bar, 24px icons, active-state pill, iOS safe-area handling.

phases.name: Dashboard cards infrastructure
phases.summary: dashboard_layouts table (per-user JSONB), base DashboardCard component, registry pattern, drag-and-drop via @dnd-kit, edit mode with add/remove.

phases.name: Dashboard cards implementation
phases.summary: Six initial card types: my_tasks, upcoming_deadlines, projects_by_phase, team_workload, personal_todos, notes.

principles: One new dependency only (@dnd-kit).
Card components must be lazy-imported.
Mobile-first dashboard grid, test at 375px.
Personal data (dashboard layouts) is per-user via RLS.

briefs.title: Mobile FAB + Phase management UI
briefs.rationale: Two small contained improvements that can ship together. FAB makes mobile task/project creation feel native; phase management UI replaces the 'edit in Supabase dashboard' workaround.

phases.name: Mobile FAB
phases.summary: Pill-style floating action button (icon + label) at bottom-center on mobile, above the tab bar. Opens a bottom sheet with a quick-add form. Per-page behaviour: Dashboard '+ Add' picker (project / task / personal todo); Year plan '+ New project'; Projects '+ New project'; Project detail '+ Add' picker (room / task); Tasks '+ New task'; Settings: none. Desktop keeps existing top-right buttons.
principles: Mobile only — do not render on desktop.
Bottom sheet uses Radix Dialog or Drawer, not a custom modal.
Quick-add forms have minimum viable fields only; full edit happens after creation.

phases.name: Phase management UI
phases.summary: Settings → Phases becomes editable for admins: add/edit/reorder/set-default/soft-delete phases. Soft delete via archived_at column. Reorder via @dnd-kit. Confirmation modal before archiving phases in use.
schema_changes: alter table phases add column archived_at timestamptz
Update all phase select queries to filter where archived_at is null (except history/audit contexts)
principles: Preset Tailwind colour palette only — no custom hex input.
Non-admins keep read-only view of phases list.
Soft delete preserves room_phase_history references.

briefs.title: Settings overhaul (sectioned) + Profile + theme + density
briefs.rationale: Settings becomes a sectioned page with proper navigation. Profile section unlocks per-user preferences. Theme support means dark mode must work end-to-end across every page — this is the meatiest part of the brief.

phases.name: Sectioned settings layout
phases.summary: Settings becomes URL-routed sections: /settings/profile, /settings/business, /settings/team, /settings/phases. Desktop: left sidebar + content area. Mobile: drill-in list (sections as tappable list, back arrow to return). /settings redirects to /settings/profile on desktop, shows list on mobile.

phases.name: Profile section
phases.summary: Current user's profile: name, avatar upload, email (read-only), sign out, plus preferences below.
schema_changes: alter table profiles add column theme_preference text default 'system' check (theme_preference in ('light', 'dark', 'system'))
alter table profiles add column density_preference text default 'comfortable' check (density_preference in ('compact', 'comfortable'))
alter table profiles add column notification_preferences jsonb default '{}'::jsonb

phases.name: Theme support + dark mode audit
phases.summary: Theme preference applied via client-side provider toggling 'dark' class on <html>. THEN: audit every existing page and component for dark mode rendering. Fix any hardcoded colours or missing token usage. This is genuinely ~30% of the brief's effort — do not skip it.
principles: Every page must work in both light and dark mode before this phase is considered done.
Use existing CSS variable tokens — do not invent new colour values.
Test at every page: dashboard, plan (both gantt and calendar), projects list, project detail, tasks, settings (all sections), login.

phases.name: Density preference
phases.summary: Compact vs comfortable: applied via root class. Affects card padding, table row height, font size by one step. Document exactly which values change in DECISIONS.md so it stays consistent.

phases.name: Team section
phases.summary: View team members. Admins can change roles only — cannot edit other people's names/avatars (users own their own profile). Notification preferences placeholder structure exists but is empty until Brief 007.

principles: Dark mode is not optional — the brief is not done until every existing page renders cleanly in dark mode.
Notification preferences schema goes in NOW (jsonb column) so Brief 007 doesn't need a migration.
Density is a smaller pass than theme but still needs to be applied consistently.

briefs.title: Room groups + per-project phase planning
briefs.rationale: Cabinet work flows by room group (Kitchen + Scullery installed together) not by individual room. This brief introduces room_groups as a third hierarchy level and adds intra-project phase scheduling visualized on a project-scoped Gantt.

phases.name: Room groups schema
phases.summary: Introduce room_groups table; rooms get nullable room_group_id. Existing rooms are 'ungrouped' until manually grouped. Update room creation flow to include group picker.
schema_changes: create table room_groups (id, project_id, name, sort_order, notes, created_at)
alter table rooms add column room_group_id uuid references room_groups(id) on delete set null
Indexes for project_id and room_group_id lookups

phases.name: Phase plans schema + auto-fill
phases.summary: phase_plans table attaching to either room_group_id OR project_id (constraint: exactly one set). Auto-fill on first open uses sensible defaults (e.g. Design 25%, Production 60%, Install 15%) distributed across whatever phases the user has configured.
schema_changes: create table phase_plans (id, room_group_id nullable, project_id nullable, phase_id, start_date, end_date, with constraint that exactly one of room_group_id or project_id is set)
Range index on (start_date, end_date)
principles: Soft warning on overlapping or out-of-order phase dates — do not block.
Auto-fill must work for any configured phase set, not hardcoded to Design/Production/Install.

phases.name: Project planning Gantt
phases.summary: New 'Planning' section on project detail page. Project-scoped Gantt: lead-time baseline at top (project start → completion), one row per room group with phase bars, one row for ungrouped rooms if any exist (showing project-level fallback). Edit via both visual drag on Gantt AND form below (table of group × phase × start × end).
principles: Visual drag and form must stay in sync — single source of truth.
Reuse the SVG Gantt approach from year-plan, do not introduce a charting library.

phases.name: Year plan integration
phases.summary: Year plan Gantt becomes expandable: tapping a project row reveals its room group sub-bars. Collapsed by default. Preserves existing year-plan UX for users who don't want the extra detail.

principles: Room groups are a hierarchy level, not a tag — proper foreign key, not a string field.
Ungrouped rooms continue to work — backward compatible with existing data.
Cascade behaviour: deleting a room group sets affected rooms to ungrouped, does not delete rooms.

briefs.title: Task system overhaul
briefs.rationale: Tasks become first-class objects rather than list rows. Many-to-many assignees, many-to-many rooms AND room groups, checklists with auto-complete, shared task templates. This is the largest single change in the roadmap.

phases.name: Schema migration
phases.summary: Migrate from single assigned_to / room_id columns to join tables. Preserve existing task data via data migration step.
schema_changes: create table task_assignees (task_id, profile_id, primary key composite)
create table task_rooms (task_id, room_id, primary key composite)
create table task_room_groups (task_id, room_group_id, primary key composite)
create table task_checklist_items (id, task_id, label, sort_order, completed_by, completed_at)
create table task_templates (id, title, description, default_priority, created_by, created_at)
create table task_template_checklist_items (id, template_id, label, sort_order)
Data migration: copy tasks.assigned_to into task_assignees; copy tasks.room_id into task_rooms
Drop columns tasks.assigned_to and tasks.room_id after migration verified
principles: Data migration is non-destructive — verify counts before dropping old columns.
RLS for personal todos updates: 'no project AND no rooms AND no room_groups' rather than current 'no project AND no room'.

phases.name: Checklist auto-complete trigger
phases.summary: Postgres trigger on task_checklist_items: when all items for a task are completed_at != null, set parent task.completed_at = now(), completed_by = whoever ticked the last item.
principles: Trigger handles the reverse too: unchecking an item un-completes the parent task.
Tasks with no checklist items continue to behave as before (manual complete).

phases.name: Task detail bottom sheet / side panel
phases.summary: Tap task row → opens detail view. Mobile: bottom sheet (Radix Drawer). Desktop: side panel sliding in from right. Shows all task fields, assignee chips, room/group chips, checklist, metadata. Edit inline.
principles: Smart room picker: groups shown at top, rooms expandable below. Selecting a group deselects its individual rooms to avoid double-linking.
Real-time updates if multiple users have the same task open (use Supabase Realtime channel on task ID).

phases.name: Task templates
phases.summary: Templates managed in Settings → new 'Templates' section. Shared team-wide. Anyone can create/edit. 'Start from template' option in quick-add flow shows template picker.
principles: Template-to-task is a one-time copy — editing template does NOT update existing tasks.
Templates can include a default checklist that gets copied in.
Common templates to seed: Quote, Cut list, Site measure, Delivery, Install.

phases.name: Query updates across app
phases.summary: All existing task queries need updating: dashboard cards (my_tasks, personal_todos), tasks page, project detail tasks list. Verify nothing references the dropped columns.

principles: This brief depends on Brief 005 (room groups) — do not start before that is merged.
Migration must preserve existing task data perfectly.
Bottom sheet / side panel pattern can be reused for project quick-view later.

briefs.title: Notifications — in-app + push
briefs.rationale: Low-noise notification system. Three triggers only: task assigned, task due today, phase changed. In-app bell icon + Web Push via VAPID (no third-party service). Email digests are deliberately deferred to Brief 008 so we can validate the in-app version is actually useful before adding email.

phases.name: Notifications schema
phases.summary: notifications table for the inbox; push_subscriptions table for per-device push endpoints. Notification preferences live on profiles.notification_preferences (jsonb column added in Brief 004).
schema_changes: create table notifications (id, user_id, type, title, body, link, read_at, created_at, dedupe_key)
create table push_subscriptions (id, user_id, endpoint, p256dh, auth, user_agent, created_at)
create index on notifications (user_id, created_at desc) where read_at is null

phases.name: Bell icon + dropdown
phases.summary: Bell icon top-right next to avatar. Badge with unread count. Dropdown shows recent notifications (latest 20). Tap notification → marks read + navigates to link. 'Mark all read' button. No auto-expire.

phases.name: PWA setup
phases.summary: manifest.json with icons + theme colours + display mode standalone. Service worker registered from root. Install prompt component (mobile only) that explains the iOS flow: Safari → Add to Home Screen → open from icon → grant permission.
principles: Document the iOS install flow clearly — users will not figure it out alone.
Service worker must handle push events even when app is not open.

phases.name: Web Push via VAPID
phases.summary: Generate VAPID keypair (one-time setup, store private key in env). Subscribe flow: user grants permission, browser returns subscription endpoint, store in push_subscriptions. Send via web-push npm library from a Vercel function. No third-party push service.
principles: Self-managed push — no OneSignal, no Firebase.
Handle stale subscriptions: if push send returns 410 Gone, delete the subscription row.

phases.name: Notification triggers
phases.summary: Three triggers only. (a) Task assigned: trigger on task_assignees insert. (b) Task due today: Vercel Cron at 06:00 local scans for tasks due today and creates notifications. (c) Phase changed: trigger on rooms.current_phase_id change, but only for users where notification_preferences.phase_changes_enabled is true.
principles: Dedupe via dedupe_key — 'task due today' for task X on date Y should only fire once.
Phase change opt-in is a single global toggle in Profile, applies to all projects.
ABSOLUTELY DO NOT add notification types beyond these three. No 'task edited', no 'comment added', no 'project viewed'. The brief must call this out explicitly.

phases.name: Preferences UI in Profile
phases.summary: Fill in the notification preferences section in Profile. Per-notification-type delivery: in-app on/off, push on/off. Phase changes: single on/off toggle.
principles: Sensible defaults: in-app ON for all three types, push OFF for all (user opts in per device by granting browser permission).
Low-noise is a CONSTRAINT, not a guideline. Three notification types. No exceptions in this brief.
In-app first, push second within the same brief — get in-app working before integrating PWA push.
iOS push requires the PWA to be installed to home screen first — there is no workaround. Document this.
All notifications must have a meaningful 'link' field for deep navigation.

briefs.title: Notifications — email digests
briefs.rationale: Daily and weekly email briefs via Resend. Strategic/summary content, not a flood. Daily is reactive (here's what's on your plate); weekly is strategic (here's the shape of your week). Built AFTER Brief 007 so we can validate the in-app experience first.

phases.name: Resend integration
phases.summary: Set up Resend account, verify a sending subdomain (e.g. notifications@your-business-domain), store API key in env, install resend SDK.

phases.name: Daily brief
phases.summary: Monday-Friday 7am via Vercel Cron. Content: tasks due today, overdue tasks, phase changes on subscribed projects since yesterday. Skip-if-empty — do not send if there is nothing to say.
principles: Fixed 7am Mon-Fri — not user configurable for v1.
Skip-if-empty is mandatory — sending an empty digest erodes trust in the feature.

phases.name: Weekly brief
phases.summary: Monday 7am. Content: projects completing this week, projects entering Production / Install this week, your open tasks grouped by project, bottlenecks (rooms stuck in a phase >2 weeks).
principles: Weekly is strategic — focus on shape-of-week, not granular activity.
Bottlenecks section is the 'management oversight' feature — make it visually prominent.

phases.name: Email preferences + unsubscribe
phases.summary: Profile gets daily-brief and weekly-brief opt-in toggles (default OFF — opt-in only). Every email has an unsubscribe link that toggles the preference for that user. One-click, no confirmation page.
principles: Default OFF — user must opt in to receive emails.
Unsubscribe is one-click — no friction.
Skip-if-empty for both daily and weekly.
Visual design of emails matters — branded header with business logo, readable on mobile, dark-mode-aware where possible.
Reuse business_info for from-name / branding in the email template.

sequencing.summary: Suggested merge order. Each brief is fully reviewed and deployed before the next is started.
dependency_notes: BRIEF_005 (room groups) MUST merge before BRIEF_006 (task overhaul) — tasks link to room groups.
BRIEF_004 adds notification_preferences column that BRIEF_007 uses — no migration needed in 007 because of this.
BRIEF_007 must merge before BRIEF_008 — email digests reuse notification subscription preferences.
BRIEF_003 (FAB + phase mgmt) is independent of later briefs and could be parallelised in theory, but recommend sequential to keep reviews simple.

items: CRM module — contacts, leads, pipeline, interactions

cross_cutting_principles: Each brief carries forward DECISIONS.md updates — friction observed during use shapes the next brief.
No new top-level dependencies unless explicitly required by a brief. Currently approved: @dnd-kit (Brief 002), web-push (Brief 007), resend (Brief 008).
Mobile-first UI testing at 375px width is required for every UI brief.
RLS must remain strict — personal data (dashboard layouts, profile prefs, personal todos, notification preferences) is per-user.
The eventual port to CabinetLogic Studio shapes some decisions — when in doubt, build the concept cleanly even if the code is throwaway.
Low-noise principle applies beyond notifications: the app should reduce work, not generate it. Resist adding 'helpful' surfaces.
